Robot Doctor Drivetrain

Controls are backwards or mixed up

Forward goes backward, turning goes the wrong way, sticks do the wrong thing. Below are the 5 most common causes on FTC robots, ordered from most to least likely, with how to check and fix each one.

Skip the guesswork — run the interactive diagnosisAbout 5 quick questions narrow this list down to your robot's actual problem.

Quick checks first

  • Is it a Logitech F310 with the green light next to MODE turned on? The small green LED next to the MODE button in the middle of the F310.
  • On a stand, does each wheel spin "forward" when you command forward? Lift the robot so the wheels are off the ground and drive forward slowly. Every wheel should turn the way that would move the robot forward.
  • If you power one named motor at a time, does the expected wheel move? Command only "frontLeft", then only "frontRight", and so on, and watch which wheel turns.
  • Does your drive code divide the powers so none go over 1? Look for a "denominator" or "max" step in the mecanum math before setPower.
  • Does the gamepad icon on the Driver Station light up when you press buttons? Top right of the Driver Station screen. Green = recognized and active, orange (SDK 12+) = unknown controller.

Common causes and how to fix them

1 A drive motor is reversed

Motors on opposite sides face opposite ways, so one side has to be reversed in code. One wrong direction makes the robot spin, drift, or strafe diagonally.

How to fix it 5 min

  1. Put the robot on a stand and command every drive motor forward at low power, one at a time.
  2. Every wheel should spin so the robot would go forward. Reverse any motor that spins backward.
  3. Some gearboxes and kits (goBILDA Strafer, REV mecanum kit) flip the direction again through gearing, so test instead of guessing.
Reverse one side
frontLeft.setDirection(DcMotorSimple.Direction.REVERSE);
backLeft.setDirection(DcMotorSimple.Direction.REVERSE);
// test each wheel on its own if anything still looks off

Sources: GM0 · Mecanum teleop · Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

2 Motor names don't match the ports

If "frontLeft" in the configuration is actually plugged in where the back-left motor is, the drive math sends power to the wrong wheels.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Run a test that powers one named motor at a time ("frontLeft" only, then "frontRight", ...) and watch which wheel actually moves.
  2. Fix either the wires or the configuration so names match the real wheel.
  3. After editing a configuration on the Driver Station, save it and make it the active configuration.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues · Pedro Pathing · Troubleshooting

3 Drive math clips or isn't compensated

Adding forward + strafe + turn can push a wheel past 1.0. The SDK clips it, which bends your direction. Strafing also needs a little extra power.

How to fix it 10 min

  1. Divide all four powers by the largest one whenever any goes over 1 (GM0's denominator trick).
  2. Multiply strafe input by about 1.1 to make up for mecanum strafe losses.
  3. Make sure forward is -gamepad.left_stick_y (the Y axis is reversed on gamepads).
GM0-style mecanum drive
double y  = -gamepad1.left_stick_y;      // forward is negative on the stick
double x  =  gamepad1.left_stick_x * 1.1; // counter imperfect strafing
double rx =  gamepad1.right_stick_x;

double denominator = Math.max(Math.abs(y) + Math.abs(x) + Math.abs(rx), 1);
frontLeft.setPower((y + x + rx) / denominator);
backLeft.setPower((y - x + rx) / denominator);
frontRight.setPower((y - x - rx) / denominator);
backRight.setPower((y + x - rx) / denominator);

Sources: GM0 · Mecanum teleop

4 Logitech MODE button is on

On the F310, MODE swaps the left stick and D-pad. The green light next to it is lit.

How to fix it 30 sec

  1. Look for the green LED next to MODE on the F310. Press MODE once to turn it off.
  2. Tape over the MODE button so nobody bumps it in a match.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues

5 Gamepad not assigned or not recognized

The Driver Station needs to know which gamepad is driver 1 vs 2, and some controllers are not supported.

How to fix it 2 min

  1. Press START + A (driver 1) or START + B (driver 2). The gamepad icon on the DS lights up green when it is active.
  2. In SDK 12+, an orange gamepad icon means the controller is not a known FTC gamepad and buttons may be mapped wrong.
  3. Run the "Test Gamepads" utility OpMode to see what each button really reports.
  4. Use a supported gamepad: Logitech F310, Xbox 360, PS4 DualShock 4, PS5 DualSense, Etpark PS4, REV PS4-compatible.
  5. Add a short USB extension that stays plugged into the Driver Station so the port does not wear out.

Sources: FTC Docs · Troubleshooting common issues · FTC Docs · Gamepad best practices
